name: Mast Cell Sarcoma

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: WHO Classification of Tumors of Hematopoietic and Lymphoid Tissues

criteria.description: Presence of highly atypical, pleomorphic mast cells with sarcomatous features on histopathological examination
Strong expression of mast cell markers CD117 (c-KIT), tryptase, and CD25 in tumor cells
Detection of activating KIT mutations, commonly D816V or other variants
Rapidly enlarging solitary mass with destructive local invasion

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation of malignant mast cells with sarcomatous features plus immunohistochemical evidence of mast cell lineage
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires exclusion of systemic mastocytosis and other mast cell neoplasms.

laboratory: Presence of atypical mast cells in biopsy specimens
Possible mild anemia or cytopenias if marrow involved
imaging: MRI or CT showing solitary soft tissue mass with bone destruction
PET scan demonstrating high metabolic activity of tumor
genetic: Other KIT exon mutations may be present
other: Immunohistochemical staining positive for CD117, tryptase, CD25
Negative for markers of other hematologic malignancies

distinguishingFeatures: High circulating mast cells in peripheral blood
Lack of mast cell markers on immunohistochemistry

redFlags: Rapidly enlarging mass with local tissue destruction
Severe anaphylactic reactions triggered by tumor manipulation
Elevated serum tryptase with atypical mast cells on biopsy
references: WHO Classification of Tumors of Hematopoietic and Lymphoid Tissues, 2017
Orphanet Report on Mast Cell Sarcoma, ORPHA:66661
Valent P et al. Mast cell sarcoma: a rare and aggressive mast cell neoplasm. Leukemia Research. 2019
